title: Vanessa Ferlito, John Carroll Lynch and Ted Levine Join Denzel Washington Thriller
excerpt:
Three actors have joined Christopher McQuarrie's untitled crime thriller.
The story follows a terminally ill former detective released from prison to face his past.
body_md:
An untitled thriller directed by Christopher McQuarrie has expanded its ensemble with Vanessa Ferlito, John Carroll Lynch and Ted Levine. The three join previously announced cast members Denzel Washington, Teyonah Parris and Miles Caton. The project is being developed by Amazon MGM Studios and United Artists.

The central character is a former police detective serving a life sentence who receives a diagnosis of terminal brain cancer. Granted compassionate release with an estimated six months left to live, he returns home hoping to reconcile with his estranged daughter and meet a grandson whose existence he had not known about. His attempt to make amends becomes increasingly difficult when elements of his troubled past return to threaten him.

The premise combines a personal story of regret and reconciliation with the mechanics of a crime thriller. The protagonist's limited remaining time raises the stakes of every decision, while the unresolved history that follows him home promises danger beyond the family drama. The announcement does not identify which characters the three newly cast actors will portray, so their exact roles in that conflict remain unknown.

McQuarrie is known for his work on the Mission: Impossible franchise and other high-profile action thrillers. Scott Barkan and Gregg Zehentner wrote the screenplay. McQuarrie and Heather McQuarrie are among the producers, alongside Scott Stuber, Nick Nesbitt, Joseph Restaino, Reza Moheet, Norman Aladjem, Katia Washington and Tommy Harper.

Ferlito's television credits include NCIS: New Orleans, Graceland, Griselda and Bookie. Lynch has appeared in American Horror Story and numerous other film and television projects. Levine is particularly recognizable from Monk and has continued working in dramatic and suspense-oriented television. Their experience in character-driven crime stories adds depth to the ensemble, although no character descriptions have been released.

The report lists an October 1 theatrical release but does not explicitly state the year in the extracted article. The exact calendar date therefore warrants separate confirmation rather than an unsupported assumption. The verified developments are the three casting additions, the creative team and the broad premise; the film's final title and further plot details remain undisclosed.
